notes:
New in 0.1.4.4 - ground that reacts to the water (sub-phase 1.4 demo):
- Erosion: fast water wears sand away (clay much more slowly; rock and concrete never). The sand travels in the water - murky brown with swirling grains - and settles where the water slows.
- Slumping: sand cannot stand steeper than 32 degrees; paint a sand wall and it slides into a pile. Clay stands almost vertical.
- Bed friction: each ground type has its real roughness.
- B: five sea bed shapes in scene 6 - rock coast, reef shelf, sandy bay with a sandbar, long gentle shelf, clay cliff.
- Run-up readout fixed: it now measures the highest ground the water actually reached (before, splash against the screen edge read as 7-10 m). Water that reaches the left edge has flooded the town and leaves the level.
- Erosion runs 30x faster than real time (a real tsunami floods for minutes, ours for seconds - coastal models do the same).
